issues.text: F6, the rows: none moved, none dropped. The LF and CR rows (O35, sweeps T1/T2) are kept because their expected side follows from the closed list of Ф2 (23 skipped characters; U+000A and U+000D are the two white-space characters that are not in it) and from 'a white-space character ends an unquoted value', not from the old isLineEnd. If REQ-ANALYST wants the sentence 'a line end is LF or CR' in the requirement, it is a wording only.

153 survivors are equivalent; one-line proofs by group (the table index is the mutant number in <scratch>/td08g/sweep/mutants.json; classes.json lists all). A (13): the constants FIND_NONE/FIND_KEEP/FIND_LITERAL and swaps NONE<->KEEP: the only reader of kind is '=== FIND_LITERAL' (findBearer, findNamedValue), so NONE and KEEP are never told apart and LITERAL stays different. B (2): findLowerAscii range A-Z extended: the image of the extra characters ('@' to '`', '[' to '{') is never a character of a list word. C (1): the record key '}' to '~' is only a name of the record. D (2): 'return -1' removed for a start that is not '$', '{' or '<': start is undefined, the loop condition is false and the function returns -1 at its end. E (3): cache hit conditions of findGroup: starts grow in one pass, so known.from <= start always holds when start <= lineEnd; start == from is impossible; start == lineEnd rescans and returns -1 at the line end at once. F (6): 'j < limit', 'j + 1 < limit', the bound of the angle group: text[limit] is the closing quote, a line end, '@', '/', white space or the end of the text, never '}', ')', '<' or '>'. G (6): name templates: a lone '$', '%' or '%%' fail the first-character test anyway; 'from += 0' rechecks a first character that is already a letter or '_'. H (11): class Z shortcuts: the Set member 'example' is covered by the substring rule (a value 'example' is word-only and contains 'example'); the length guards, the '| 32' prefilter, the bound of the 'your' compare (a 4-character read past a shorter value meets a terminator, never 'r'), 'return false' removed (undefined is falsy), the loop start at the character before the value (a sign or a space, never 'e'). I (15): path and call: an empty identifier gives false whatever follows (-1, -2, 0 as 'no separator'); the '?.' bound checks read text[b] which is a terminator, never '.'; return values used as booleans. J (8): bare names: prev starts below 97 in any case, c and prev are letters or '_' when they are compared (the bounds 90/91, 96/97, 122/123 are not letters), the keyword length cap 9 instead of 8 (the Set decides). K (11): a backslash directly before a line end or the end of an unclosed string: the value is literal in both versions (it ends with the backslash), so the file is refused either way; the position after the closing quote differs only by one character that is a quote or the last character of the content, never the start of a name; an escaped closing quote is held by the rows with ${a\"b}. L (7): closers: with an opener of the same kind in the value nothing that is kept changes when more or fewer closers are dropped ($(..) stays a call, a call stays a call; V4 needs no closer of the kind at all); 'kind -1 to 0' consumes one unit of the counter of ')' for a non-closer, so the walk can never get across it (the units run out one short). M (12): the end-of-text sentinel (10 / 9 / 11 / '<= n'): an empty value at the end of the text is NONE for any of them; the early returns are repeated by the next test. N (30): initial indexes (-1 or +1 where indexOf or lastIndex clamps), 'at + 10 +- 1' and 'at + 3 +- 1' (the next occurrence cannot start inside the marker, and a start inside a run is skipped anyway), '< n' read as '<= n' (charCodeAt(n) is NaN, no class contains it), the leftmost-dot walk of the JWT (the next character of a dot pair gives the same 'empty'), and the first-character recount. O (6): the i flag of the pattern for Bearer makes A-Z and a-z the same set, so removing or shrinking one range is invisible. P (8): a quote at the very end of the text opens an empty string: NONE with or without the 'closing quote' shortcut. Q (12): the minimum / maximum length of a name and of a scheme word and the 'return -1' of the last-letter filter: the sets (the seven names, the nine schemes) decide, the bounds only save time.

13 survivors: the requirement is silent. Ф5 says only: 'ghp_, gho_, ghs_ и не менее 20 знаков, github_pat_ и не менее 20' - no set of characters. The code takes [A-Za-z0-9] (and '_' for github_pat_) as the old rule M5 did. Mutants that widen a range of the body by one character ('@', '[', '`', '{', '/', ':') or remove '_' from the github_pat_ body (1407, 1408, 1412, 1413, 1417, 1418, 1454, 1455, 1459, 1460, 1464, 1465, 1466) change the answer only for a body with such a character in it, and no sentence of the requirement says which side is right; the sweeps K2-K5 test letters and digits (refused: shrinking ranges is red). The same silence: a leading dot before a JWT (sweep J1 leaves '.' out), as in 08c. If the owner wants the set named, it is one sentence in Ф5.

Two survivors are performance-only (the record of failed group searches in findGroup: 283 'known.from >= start', 286 'return -1' of the cache removed): the answers are the same, the time becomes quadratic.
